_readme: CURATOR-OWNED. No pipeline writes this file. scripts/export_repository_site.py owns repository.json beside it and overwrites that file on every run, so any prose kept there would be destroyed by the next export. Everything a person writes lives here instead, and this is the file to edit to change the words on the landing page. No count is ever stored: numbers are written as {tokens} that the page fills from the payload at load, so this file cannot go stale against the corpus.
_tokens: Usable anywhere in intro prose. {records} how many records. {yearMin} {yearMax} the publication range. {themes} how many finance themes. {sourceTypes} how many kinds of source. {organizations} how many organizations are named. {recentFrom} the first year of the recent window. {recentShare} the share published from that year onward, as a percentage. An unknown token is left on the page as written, so a typo is visible rather than silent.
_removed_2026_09_16: Three blocks were REMOVED on curator instruction, along with the page sections that read them: start_here (foundational reading), questions (question-led saved views) and lab_outputs (the Lab and partner feed). They are not lost and are not to be restored on the assumption that they went missing. The shapes they used are recorded in site/README.md so the decision can be reversed deliberately rather than reconstructed.

intro.beta: Beta release. The collection is growing and some records are still being reviewed, so expect gaps and the occasional rough edge. Please review the underlying research before making decisions.
intro.lede: Academic research, case studies, deal profiles, and media coverage on how risk reduction and resilience gets funded and financed. Built for practitioners, including project proponents, underwriters, and capital allocators, who need to know what has and hasn't worked before and why and want to know more about the cutting edge of resilience finance.

blocks.heading: What's included
blocks.body: The repository currently contains {records} records published between {yearMin} and {yearMax}, drawn from {organizations} organizations and sorted into {themes} finance themes. Each record includes a summary of the underlying material, key points, who is named in it, and a link to the original document. Access to the repository is free, although some documents may sit behind a paywall and are flagged as such.

blocks.heading: The range of sources is deliberate
blocks.body: Useful material is not only found in academic journals. A rating agency's downgrade note, a trade publication's account of a catastrophe bond, a city's own funding memo, or a podcast can all contain useful information, often published ahead of the academic review cycle. The repository includes many types of sources, all labeled clearly to allow users to sort and evaluate.

criteria.heading: What's included and why
criteria.lede: Before a document is included in the repository, it's scored on four metrics. The repository uses a combination of curator selection and AI to source documents. All summaries and insights are extracted and generated by AI; remember to use caution when referencing the material.

items.term: It is about resilience or risk reduction
items.gloss: The document is focused on reducing risk and building resilience to physical climate risk. Work on cutting emissions and mitigation is a different field and is not collected here unless it bears directly on resilience or risk reduction.

items.term: It is relevant to the US
items.gloss: The document centers US-focused work, or international work that could transfer to a US context. There is much to learn from international work on resilience and risk reduction, which is why a large share of the collection is not US-specific.

An instrument, a transaction, a price signal, a funding route, a return. Engineering or policy description on its own is not enough, however good it is: the gap this collection exists to close is the financial one.

items.term: It is recent enough to be useful
items.gloss: The repository covers the last 15 years, with higher priority given to recent years: {recentShare} of the collection was published from {recentFrom} onward. Older work is kept where it is still the reference everyone cites.

updates.heading: How we keep the repository current
updates.body: New material is sourced continuously and reviewed by the Lab before being added each week. This page is a snapshot as of the date at the top of the page.

why_this_matters.note: Per-record curator voice, keyed by NNN as a string, shown at the top of the expanded card. A record with no entry here shows no block, which is the correct empty state: the machine never writes this field, so an absence means nobody has written it rather than that the value is unknown.

feedback.note: Where a reader's report goes. `mailto` is deliberate: the site is static, has no backend and makes no third-party request, and a form service would need an account, a secret in the deploy and would send the reader's report through somebody else. Change `email` here and it changes everywhere, including the offline bundle. Remove this block entirely and the links simply do not appear.
feedback.record_label: Report a problem with this record
feedback.page_label: Report a problem with this page or a record
feedback.intro: Please describe the problem in a sentence or two, then send. The lines below tell us which record and which version of the site you were looking at.
